entities.name: SoftBank Group
entities.desc: Japan's #1 company by market cap as of June 2026 (¥47.2T, +73% YTD), displacing Toyota. ARM Holdings (~90% stake) accounts for ~60% of NAV. Sovereign AI cloud platform for Japanese government and regulated institutions — NVIDIA H100 clusters in Tokyo & Osaka. Lead sponsor of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (30+ firm consortium, ¥1T NEDO backing). **SB OAI Japan GK (Issue #18, Jun 2026):** SoftBank-OpenAI JV launched 'Patching as a Service' — AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation for Japan's top 3,000 companies, starting with critical infrastructure (airports, power grids, transit). 50 security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Son Masayoshi framed AI-powered cyberattacks as a 'Black Ships' (黒船) moment — national crisis framing positions SoftBank for METI government procurement contracts. First revenue signal expected August 2026 earnings. **Roze spinout (#28):** AI-robotics spinout targeting $100B US IPO; bundles ABB Robotics ($5.4B), Ampere Computing ($6.5B), DigitalBridge ($3B); analyst day targeted July 2026. **OpenAI IPO delay (#27):** Stock fell 13% Jun 26, 2026 on NYT report of possible IPO delay to 2027; cumulative OpenAI exposure ~$64.6B (~13% stake). **Tranche II (#32):** Second $10B deployment into OpenAI July 1, 2026; SFTBY -4.52%; Tranche III contractually Oct 1, 2026. **Noetra (#31):** SoftBank leads Japan sovereign physical AI consortium (¥387.3B METI commitment); engineers seconded alongside PFN; also largest foreign OpenAI investor — dual-role tension as sovereign AI competition intensifies.

entities.name: NEC Corporation
entities.desc: Japan's largest system integrator. Anthropic's first Japan-based Global Partner; deploying Claude Opus across ~30,000 NEC Group engineers via BluStellar Scenario platform. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Runs dual-stack hedge: backs sovereign domestic model while distributing Claude for enterprise and government — SOC services for finance, manufacturing, and local government sectors. **Noetra consortium (#17, #29, #31):** Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) with >10% equity stake alongside SoftBank, Sony, Honda. Pattern setter for Japanese IT integrators to add domestic model exposure alongside US frontier models.

entities.name: Fujitsu
entities.desc: Japan's largest IT services firm. **Dual frontier AI partnership (May 27, 2026):** Signed resale + integration agreements with both OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex) and Anthropic (Claude) — largest Japanese IT integrator now official dual-frontier AI distributor covering government ministries and enterprise. Sets the pattern for NEC, Hitachi, NTT to follow. **AI Foundation Model Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. — brings government and enterprise customer distribution to the domestic model project. Also member of MHI + PFN + Fujitsu supply chain for defense/critical infrastructure AI. **Dual AI partnership (#4, May 2026):** Reseller for both OpenAI (ChatGPT Enterprise, Codex) and Anthropic (Claude) across government ministries and enterprise clients. **Noetra consortium (#17, #29, #31):** Equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Dev Co. (Noetra); brings government distribution + enterprise client base. **FSA compliance beneficiary (#24, #26):** Positioned for Q3 contract acceleration as non-compliant foreign-API routers face regulatory exposure.

entities.name: Sony AI
entities.desc: Sony Group AI subsidiary. Member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). Research focus covers robotics, gaming AI, and imaging intelligence. Sony's hardware ecosystem (PlayStation, cameras, sensors) provides unique data sources for physical AI training.

entities.name: Preferred Networks (PFN)
entities.zh: プリファードネットワークス
entities.desc: Japan's leading deep learning AI startup. PLaMo foundation models, MN-Core AI processors, PFCP cloud platform. Engineers seconded to SoftBank physical AI JV (announced April 2026). **MHI + PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. PFN contributes PLaMo models and MN-Core AI processors; MHI contributes aerospace, defense, and energy hardware. Policy framing: Japan-made AI for keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) domains. Capital alliance with MHI targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027). **PLaMo 3.0 Prime (#25, Jun 22 2026):** ¥60 input / ¥250 output per million tokens — less than half comparable US model pricing; trained from scratch on Japanese-heavy data (no foreign base model fine-tune). AI sovereignty (AI主権) framing: FSA audit-trail compliance built-in; targeted at Japan's 3.8M SMBs, financial services, healthcare. **Noetra (#31):** Engineers seconded to SoftBank-led sovereign AI consortium alongside separate MHI defense AI track (#7).

entities.name: NTT Research
entities.desc: Research arm of NTT Group (日本電信電話). Quantum and AI research; Rapidus investor in ¥267.6B funding round. NTT is Japan's national telecom incumbent — provides critical infrastructure for data center connectivity underpinning Japan's AI ambitions.

entities.name: Noetra (Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co.)
entities.zh: 日本AIファウンデーションモデル開発 / Noetra
entities.desc: SoftBank-led sovereign physical AI consortium backed by METI ¥387.3B (five-year; largest single domestic AI commitment in Japan's history). Engineers seconded from SoftBank and Preferred Networks (PFN); AIST providing research coordination. 40+ manufacturing companies committed, including Yaskawa Electric, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Electric, Tokyo Electron, Asahi Kasei, Daiwa House, SG Holdings. **Goal:** Multimodal physical AI (フィジカルAI) foundation model for robot and industrial machinery control; first model targeted FY2026 (by March 2027); annual updates from manufacturer production-floor data. **Noetra capital close (#29, Jun 29-30 2026):** Second investor tranche (~10 firms) including MUFG, Mizuho, SMBC, Nippon Steel, Kobe Steel, Asahi Kasei, Yaskawa, Fujitsu — total ~34 member organizations. **Competition framing:** Not benchmarking against GPT-4o; competing on physical AI workloads, sovereign data residency, Japanese-language precision, FSA/METI compliance-native architecture. Structural edge: only model trained on Fanuc, Toyota, Kawasaki industrial telemetry foreign models cannot access. NEDO government funding: up to ¥1T over five years (FY2026–FY2030).

entities.name: Rapidus
entities.desc: Japan's state-backed 2nm logic semiconductor project. IPA Capital Round #3 completed June 5, 2026: ¥150B new capital from IPA (METI agency). Cumulative IPA capital: ¥274.95B. Total funding (all sources): ¥424.95B (IPA equity + ¥167.6B from 32 private co-investors including Canon, Fujitsu, NTT, SoftBank, Sony, Development Bank of Japan). Total government commitment estimate: ~¥2.35T across all instruments. Target: full-scale 2nm manufacturing by 2027 at IIM-1 fab, Chitose, Hokkaido. Key open risk: no external customer supply commitment disclosed — needs hyperscaler or sovereign AI anchor customer. **Total government commitment (#23):** Approaching ¥3T (¥150B June IPA equity + ¥631.5B April + prior rounds). 2nm GAA transistors confirmed July 2025. Target: 25,000 wafer starts/month at full ramp; mass production FY2027. Key open risk: design-win pipeline beyond Tenstorrent remains thin — commercial viability unproven without broader customer commitments by Q3/Q4 2026.

entities.name: TSMC JASM (Kumamoto)
entities.desc: TSMC-majority JV in Kumamoto, Kyushu. Partners: Sony Group, Toyota, Denso. JASM-1: 6–12nm, production ramping 2024. JASM-2: upgraded to 3nm (approved April 2026), $17B total investment, government covers ~50%. Production target: 2028. Positions Kyushu as Japan's high-end semiconductor cluster alongside Rapidus Hokkaido. Serves automotive AI chip demand (Toyota, Honda, Denso supply chain).

entities.name: Kioxia
entities.desc: Japan's leading NAND flash memory manufacturer. Yokkaichi + Kitakami (北上) fabs. Cost per wafer ~$2,000 vs ~$4,000 Samsung, ~$6,000 Micron/SK Hynix — structural advantage through BiCS9. UBS initiated with Buy at ¥79,000 target (May 2026). Entire 2026 NAND output sold out. Q2 operating profit projected ¥1.3T — above full-year FY2025 record. BiCS10 (332-layer) will equalize cost advantage; UBS calls it a 12–18-month trade window. VLSI June 14: MSA-CBA 1,000-layer NAND demonstration.

entities.name: Tokyo Electron (TEL)
entities.desc: Japan's largest semiconductor equipment maker. Critical supplier of etch, deposition, and cleaning equipment to TSMC, Samsung, Rapidus. Under pressure from US export controls on advanced tool categories. Key beneficiary of Japan's semiconductor manufacturing renaissance. **Nikkei 225 record 72,648 (#23, Jun 22 2026):** TEL price ~¥36,000 → ~10% Nikkei index weight (price-weighted); TEL + Advantest contributed 840+ index points on Jun 22 alone. AI infrastructure investment thesis (Microsoft $10B, AWS ¥2.3T) drives foreign inflows (~¥16T since Apr 2025). TEL Q1 FY2027 earnings (late July): primary readthrough for Rapidus, JASM, Micron Hiroshima equipment order velocity. Also member of Noetra manufacturing coalition (#31).

entities.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
entities.desc: World's largest silicon wafer producer; critical input to TSMC Kumamoto and Rapidus Hokkaido. Also Japan's leading PVC producer. Semiconductor wafer division provides ~70% of silicon wafers used by leading-edge foundries globally.

entities.name: Fanuc
entities.desc: Japan's largest industrial robot and CNC machine maker. May 2026: announced Google Gemini integration enabling natural-language factory control — all future Fanuc robots will be compatible with Google software. Consortium member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. METI physical AI initiative beneficiary. Key robotics data contributor for Japan's sovereign 物理AI model. **AI Robotics Strategy (#32, Jul 1 2026):** Named as primary OEM supply-chain beneficiary in Japan Revised AI Robotics Strategy (10M AI-equipped robots by 2040 across 18 sectors). Robot deployment gated on Noetra foundation model readiness.

entities.name: Yaskawa Electric
entities.desc: Top-3 industrial robot maker globally. **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Strategic significance: Yaskawa's production-floor automation data feeds directly into foundation model training pipeline — validates 'physical AI' framing as structural, not marketing. Core factory automation and motion control product lines remain primary revenue. **Noetra equity stake (#17, #29, #31):** Formal commitment to Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra); equity stake signals downstream deployment of physical AI models in Yaskawa Motoman systems. Motoman brand: ~20% global collaborative robot market share. Yaskawa's production-floor telemetry data feeds Noetra training pipeline — demand-side validation of the physical AI thesis. One of three primary OEM supply-chain beneficiaries named in Japan Revised AI Robotics Strategy (#32).

entities.name: JAL × GMO Humanoid Trial (Haneda)
entities.zh: JAL × GMO AI＆ロボティクス
entities.desc: Japan Airlines and GMO AI & Robotics launched a two-year Unitree G1 humanoid robot trial at Haneda Airport in 2026 for baggage, cargo, and cabin operations. First cycle-time data from week of June 1. METI June liability guidelines will be the policy gate determining how quickly pilots convert into scaled commercial operations.

entities.name: Honda Motor
entities.desc: Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (10%+ equity). First designated external deployer of the sovereign physical AI model. Long AI/robotics history (ASIMO humanoid). AI Foundation Model Consortium capital round closing June 2026. Woven City (Toyota JV) adjacent AI infrastructure investment. **Noetra consortium (#29, #31):** Founding member of Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) with >10% equity stake alongside SoftBank, NEC, Sony. Contributes automotive/mobility telemetry to physical AI training pipeline.

entities.name: Nippon Steel
entities.desc: Japan's largest steelmaker. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV consortium (June 2026 capital round). Materials science data (steel properties, processing conditions) key training input for physical AI foundation model. Represents heavy industry capital backing Japan's sovereign AI ambitions.

entities.name: Asahi Kasei
entities.desc: Diversified Japanese chemical and materials conglomerate (TSE: 3407). **AI Foundation Consortium (Issue #17):** Confirmed equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. Materials and healthcare data assets are likely AI training contribution. Earlier covered in the context of industrial AI adoption (Issues #4, #5). **Noetra consortium (#17, #31):** Joined Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra) as an equity member; spans materials science, synthetic fibers, healthcare; production-process data contributes to Noetra training pipeline.

entities.name: MUFG (Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group)
entities.desc: Japan's largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized to deploy dual AI cyber stack: Anthropic Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 in tandem. Part of FSA working group on AI-related cyber risks (36 entities, 15 critical infrastructure sectors). Each 25bp BOJ rate hike adds ~¥100–150B in annual net interest income across the three megabanks. **Noetra consortium (#29, Jun 29-30 2026):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (Noetra); part of second investor tranche (tens of millions of yen). FSA AI compliance guidelines (#24, #26) create dual obligation as both compliance subject and potential procurement beneficiary.

entities.name: Mizuho Financial Group
entities.zh: みずほフィナンシャルグループ
entities.desc: Japan's third-largest bank. Committed to Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV (June 2026). Government-authorized for dual Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5 AI cyber stack. BOJ rate normalization is structurally bullish for NII expansion. **Noetra consortium (#29):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (second investor tranche). FSA AI compliance guidelines take effect July 1, 2026.

entities.name: SMBC (Sumitomo Mitsui Banking)
entities.desc: Japan's second-largest bank. Government-authorized for dual AI cyber stack alongside MUFG and Mizuho. FSA working group participant. BOJ rate hike of 25bp adds ~¥100–150B NII across the three megabanks. **Noetra consortium (#29):** Small equity stake in Japan AI Foundation Model Development Co. (second investor tranche). FSA AI compliance guidelines take effect July 1, 2026.

entities.name: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
entities.desc: Japan's central bank. Governor: Kazuo Ueda (植田和男). Policy rate: 0.75% (held April 2026, 6–3 vote split). Raised FY2026 core CPI forecast to 2.8% from 1.9%. OIS pricing June 2026: 77% probability of 25bp hike to 1.00% at June 15–16 MPM. Three dissenters favoured immediate hike. OECD projects 2.0% by end-2027. JGB purchase commitment signal at June MPM is the key 'hawkish rates / dovish duration' watch. **Q2 2026 Tankan (#31, #32, Jul 1 2026):** Large manufacturer DI +22 (vs. +16 consensus; beat by 6 pts; highest since 2018). Non-manufacturer DI +37 (highest since 1991). Capex actual +11.5% FY2026/27. Recurring profits guidance -6.7% (capex-despite-margin-pressure confirms automation bet). BOJ raised policy rate to 1.00% Jun 16; July 30-31 MPM next key date. AI-specific survey items added in 2026 Tankan — first explicit capex monitoring for AI infrastructure.

entities.name: Ministry of Finance (MoF)
entities.desc: Japan's fiscal authority. Finance Minister: Satsuki Katayama. Authorized record ¥11.73T (~$74B) FX intervention (為替介入) April 28–May 27, 2026 — first since July 2024, surpassing prior monthly record. USD/JPY hit ¥155 then retraced to 159.3. Issued fresh verbal warnings June 2026. 300bp US-Japan rate gap drives structural yen carry trade pressure.

entities.name: METI (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
entities.desc: Japan's industrial policy ministry. Core AI infrastructure funder and semiconductor strategist. ¥1.23T AI/semiconductor budget envelope; ¥387.3B specifically for AI development. Backs Rapidus 2nm semiconductor project (~¥2.35T total government commitment). AI Promotion Act (AI推進法): enacted 2026, innovation-first, voluntary guidelines for most applications. **Genesis Mission (Issue #11, Jun 4–5, 2026):** Japan named first international partner in U.S. DOE Genesis Mission — $1B combined ($500M each) over 5 years; 12 U.S. national labs + 12 Japanese research institutions; quantum technology, nuclear fusion, biotechnology, materials AI, advanced manufacturing. MEXT co-sponsoring. **AI Basic Plan revision (Issue #22, Jun 20, 2026):** Draft revision released for public comment — adds enhanced international cooperation provisions and new cybersecurity plank on AI-enabled cyberattacks. Cabinet approval sought at early date; cybersecurity budget line likely to follow. **Noetra / ¥387.3B commitment (#31):** Largest single domestic AI commitment in Japan's history; ¥300B separately allocated to AI foundation models in FY2026 budget; Noetra's ¥387.3B exceeds prior NEDO AI programs by several multiples. **Revised AI Robotics Strategy (#32, Jul 1 2026):** 10 million AI-equipped robots across 18 sectors by 2040; gated on Noetra model readiness. **FSA AI compliance (#24):** Joint finalization of AI workflow guidelines effective July 1, 2026.

entities.name: NEDO
entities.zh: 新エネルギー・産業技術総合開発機構
entities.py: Shin'enerugī Sangyō Gijutsu Sōgō Kaihatsu Kikō
entities.desc: New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization. Executing Japan's ¥1T AI fund (FY2026–FY2031). Approved Rapidus FY2026 plan (PDK general release + chiplet pilot). Expected FY2026 budget allocation for Rapidus 2nm delayed from May, now due June week 1. Administers public-private designation for Japan AI Foundation Model Development JV. **Noetra funding (#31):** Formal co-announcement with METI of ¥387.3B five-year commitment to Noetra physical AI consortium. NEDO ¥1T total over FY2026–FY2030 (government funding component of Noetra). Research coordination alongside AIST (産業技術総合研究所).

tags.l: Physical AI: first model FY2026 target

entities.name: Digital Agency (デジタル庁)
entities.desc: Established 2021. Leads Japan's digital transformation. Government Gennai (ゲンナイ) generative AI platform launched nationwide May 2026 — government-wide AI deployment. **APPI Amendment (Issue #12, Jun 2026):** Personal Information Protection Act amendment passed lower house; removes individual consent requirement for AI training on medical histories and criminal records. Digital Minister Matsumoto Hisashi used 'AI colony' (AIの植民地) framing — data deregulation as national sovereignty issue. Bill in upper house debate; must clear before parliament rises July 2026. No civil-remedy mechanism — key risk. Primary beneficiaries if passes: healthcare AI, insurance underwriting, enterprise NLP. **APPI revision (#12, #30):** Bill cleared Lower House May 2026; Upper House vote before July 17 Diet recess; allows AI training on pseudonymized personal data without individual consent; Digital Agency / PPC joint review board. Primary beneficiary: Noetra physical AI consortium. **Data center siting (#23):** No MLIT/METI response to Chiba lawsuits as of June 2026; any zoning legislation requires prioritization before Diet recess.

tags.l: Data center siting: no response yet

entities.name: FSA (Financial Services Agency)
entities.desc: Japan's financial regulator. Launched public-private working group on AI-related cyber risks: 36 entities across 15 critical infrastructure sectors. Authorized Japan's three megabanks (MUFG, SMBC, Mizuho) to deploy dual AI cyber stack (Claude Mythos + OpenAI G-5.5). AI cyber governance framework in development. **AI workflow compliance guidelines (#24, #26, #30, Jun 22 2026):** Mandatory audit trails (監査証跡), explainability (説明可能性), and continuous model risk assessment for financial services, healthcare, energy, critical infrastructure. Three-month grace period ended July 1, 2026. Enforcement phase began July 1; examination findings expected Q3 2026 disclosures. Operationalizes AI Promotion Act (AI推進法, passed May 2025) into sector-specific mandates — first enforceable teeth in a major regulated sector.

entities.name: SB OAI Japan GK
entities.zh: SBオープンエーアイジャパン
entities.desc: SoftBank-OpenAI joint venture, established November 2025. **Patching as a Service (launched June 17, 2026):** AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation. Phase 1 target: Japan's top 3,000 companies, focusing on critical infrastructure (airports, power grids, public transit). Technology: OpenAI's specialized cybersecurity models for vulnerability identification; advisory only (not automated code deployment). 50 dedicated security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Also operates Sarashina API service (launched Nov 2025). Positioned for METI government procurement contracts alongside commercial enterprise revenue. First revenue signal expected in SoftBank August 2026 quarterly earnings. **Patching as a Service (#18, Jun 17 2026):** Commercial launch of AI-powered enterprise vulnerability assessment and remediation planning. Phase 1: Japan's top 3,000 companies, focus on airports, power grids, public transit. 50 dedicated security specialists at launch; target 1,000 personnel. Advisory only (not automated code deployment). Son framed AI cyberattacks as 'Black Ships' (黒船) moment. First revenue signal expected August 2026 quarterly earnings. **OpenAI IPO delay context (#27):** SB OAI Japan GK commercial revenue narrative is SoftBank's partial earnings decoupling argument from Vision Fund marks.

tags.l: Patching as a Service: commercial Jun 2026

entities.name: PKSHA Technology
entities.desc: Tokyo-based AI software company (TSE: 3993). Bridges academic AI research and enterprise deployment in Japan. **Japan AI Index partnership (Issue #10, Jun 4, 2026):** Co-founding partner (with University of Tokyo + Anthropic) of the first Japan AI Index — fixed-point observation framework tracking AI's impact on employment, industries, economy, and education. First report October–November 2026; updates every 3–6 months. PKSHA's structural link to Japanese corporate sector makes it the enterprise deployment conduit for the index's findings. Creates the first credible, non-self-reported AI adoption data series for Japan. **Japan AI Index (#10, Jun 4 2026):** Three-way partnership with University of Tokyo and Anthropic; Claude usage telemetry cross-referenced with MIC/Cabinet Office statistics; first report October-November 2026; designed for comparison with Stanford AI Index and OECD digital adoption metrics. PKSHA bridges research and enterprise deployment.

entities.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI)
entities.desc: Japan's largest defense and heavy industry manufacturer (TSE: 7011). Aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial systems. **PFN Business Alliance (Issue #7, Jun 2, 2026):** Alliance signed with Preferred Networks for joint development of AI for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. MHI contributes aerospace/defense/energy hardware + system integration expertise; PFN contributes PLaMo foundation models and MN-Core AI processors. Use cases: autonomous situational assessment, predictive maintenance, rapid crisis response in high-reliability environments. Policy framing: keizai anzenhoshō (経済安全保障, economic security) — defense customers prefer domestic supply chains. Capital alliance targeted within FY2026 (by March 2027). ITO corporate strategy framework guiding integration. **PFN business alliance (#7, Jun 2 2026):** Capital and business alliance with Preferred Networks (capital stake targeted within FY2026). Scope: joint AI development for mission-critical machinery — social infrastructure + national security/defense. PFN contributes PLaMo foundation models, MN-Core AI processors, PFCP cloud; MHI contributes aerospace, defense, energy hardware. Explicitly framed as Japan-made AI for keizai anzenhoshō (economic security, 経済安全保障) — defense customers prefer domestic supply chains.

tags.l: Economic security (経済安全保障) framing

entities.name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
entities.desc: Kobe-based heavy industry conglomerate: aerospace, defense, energy, and industrial robots. One of Japan's three primary OEM supply-chain beneficiaries named in the July 1, 2026 Revised AI Robotics Strategy (10M AI-equipped robots by 2040 across 18 sectors, #32). **Noetra coalition (#31):** Participating in METI ¥387.3B physical AI consortium led by SoftBank; production-floor automation data contributes to training pipeline. **Humanoid robot program (#5):** Active development of full-size humanoid robotic systems for manufacturing and hazardous-environment use. Cross-reference: Issue #32 (AI robotics strategy OEM list); Issue #31 (Noetra coalition member); Issue #5 (humanoid robot program).

entities.name: Mitsubishi Electric
entities.desc: Tokyo. Major electrical equipment and factory automation maker; MELFA industrial robot arm line is a key product. **Noetra coalition (#31):** Member of METI ¥387.3B physical AI consortium; factory automation telemetry from MELFA systems contributes to physical AI training pipeline. Alongside Yaskawa and Kawasaki, forms the core of Japan's industrial robot supply chain feeding into the Noetra model.

entities.name: Sakura Internet
entities.zh: さくらインターネット
entities.desc: Osaka. Japan's leading domestic GPU cloud and data center operator. **AI sovereign cloud (#23, #25):** Named as likely domestic hosting channel for on-premises PLaMo (Preferred Networks) deployments; also partner with Microsoft's $10B Japan AI infrastructure commitment (2026–2029). Structural positioning: sole major GPU cloud operator entirely under Japanese data-residency jurisdiction — critical for FSA compliance-native AI deployments where foreign cloud routing is unacceptable. Cross-reference: Issue #23 (Microsoft/AWS Japan investment context); Issue #25 (PLaMo 3.0 Prime indirect beneficiary).

entities.name: NTT Data
entities.desc: Tokyo. Japan's largest IT services company by revenue (subsidiary of NTT Group). **FSA compliance beneficiary (#25, #26, #30):** Named alongside Preferred Networks PLaMo as a primary structural beneficiary of FSA AI workflow compliance guidelines (effective July 1, 2026) — domestically governed models with native Japanese-jurisdiction audit architecture are positioned for Q3 contract acceleration as non-compliant foreign-API routers face regulatory exposure. **Enterprise AI distribution (#25):** Positioned as enterprise deployment partner for PLaMo 3.0 Prime, bringing established government and financial-sector customer base at scale — capabilities PFN is still building. Cross-reference: Issue #11 (NTT Research quantum/photonics DOE relationship); Issue #25 (PLaMo 3.0 Prime distribution beneficiary); Issue #26, #30 (FSA compliance catalyst).

entities.name: Colt Technology Services
entities.zh: コルト・テクノロジー・サービス
entities.desc: London HQ. Data center developer and network provider. **Inzai data center lawsuit (#23, Jun 21 2026):** Colt's 52-meter data center in Inzai City, Chiba Prefecture (SPV backed by Mitsui & Co., CPP Investments Canada, Fidelity) triggered first data center lawsuit in Japan. Adjacent to a 15-story residential condo; ~25% documented property value decline. Inzai City admitted current rules cannot address the conflict. **Broader implication:** Lawsuit filed alongside Shiroi City (2 suits) and opposition clusters in Saitama, Akishima, Hino, Kodaira, and Tokyo's Koto Ward — establishes legal precedent for Tokyo-metro data center site selection risk. METI/MLIT response pending before Diet recess (Jul 2026). Cross-reference: Issue #23 (Japan AI Basic Plan pledge to be 'most AI-friendly' vs. community rights tension).

tags.l: Inzai: first DC lawsuit in Japan

entities.name: AIST
entities.desc: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology. METI-affiliated research agency. **Noetra research coordination (#31):** AIST providing research coordination for METI's ¥387.3B Noetra physical AI consortium (SoftBank-led); alongside NEDO, one of two government-side research anchors. Primary missions include AI, robotics, materials science, and energy technology — directly aligned with Noetra's physical AI and manufacturing automation thesis. Cross-reference: Issue #31 (Noetra formal announcement).
